VKF 0.1.6 — Strict Vector Lifting And Axis Reductions

VKF 0.1.6 replaces compatibility-filtered aggregate broadcasting with a smaller, stricter rule: ordinary typed functions may lift recursively through vectors, while tuples and records remain explicit whole values.

What changed from 0.1.5

  • Automatic lifting descends only through fixed or dynamic vector layers.
  • A lifted element must match the function parameter type exactly. Ordinary scalar conversions still apply to direct calls, but do not select vector leaves.
  • Tuples and records are atomic. Their arithmetic requires an explicit operator overload instead of silently transforming selected fields.
  • Exact whole-container matches still take priority. A row function can therefore map over a matrix without a user-written loop.
  • Unary and binary overload families are resolved from typed aliases before machine lowering. The backend no longer guesses that an arbitrary aggregate should use an unrelated overload.
  • Higher-order callables and generic multiset containers retain safe, arity-aware overload fallback when their frontend representation is erased.
  • stat.sum reduces all nested vector dimensions when axis is omitted.
  • stat.sum(axis:) accepts one constant integer or a nonempty tuple of constant integers for fixed rectangular numeric vectors. Negative axes count from the last dimension; duplicates and out-of-range axes are compile errors.
  • Sum results retain the numeric vector leaf type when it is statically known.
  • Landing-page benchmark tables now present measurements and same-host ratios without exposing internal acceptance thresholds or pass labels.
  • Relative performance targets remain available as explicit development checks; release evidence collection does not turn runner-specific ratios into a correctness verdict.

Verification

  • 320 native VKF tests pass with zero failures.
  • The suite includes explicit rejection coverage for tuple/record lifting, conversion-selected vector leaves, implicit record arithmetic, duplicate and out-of-range axes, and tuple arguments to stat.sum.
  • Positive coverage includes fixed and dynamic vector lifting, nested vectors, vector-of-record calls, row functions over matrices, recursive full sums, integer/negative/tuple axes, alias-aware overloads, integer variadic sums, resource ownership, and multiset arithmetic.
  • All 59 documented programs are rebuilt and executed as part of release proof.
  • Windows x64, Linux x64, and macOS ARM64 proof reports bind outputs and timing samples to exact source and compiler hashes.
  • The latest same-host Linux comparison and 256-policy Windows landscape are retained with the release evidence, including every timing sample and code hash.

Native scope

The included native modules remain math, stat, random, time, io, collections, errors, system, process, and regex. physics, ui, and symbolic remain excluded rather than shipping partial implementations.
